headings.title: Life imprisonment without parole until thirty years served
headings.reviewNote: Mandates authorized term of life imprisonment without eligibility for probation or parole until offender has served at least thirty years.

entries.reviewSummary: Dual-version entry (H.B. 2637 & 3155, 2026; Revisor note states effective 1-01-28); subsection 3 removes section 558.019(4) exclusion and natural-life sentence.

headings.title: Definition and elements of sexual trafficking of a child in the second degree
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense as recruiting, harboring, causing, or advertising child under eighteen to participate in commercial sex, sexual performance, or explicit material.

headings.title: Belief of child's age of eighteen or older not a defense
headings.reviewNote: Provides that defendant's belief that child was eighteen years of age or older is not a defense.

headings.title: Felony penalty ranges, mandatory minimum for force, and natural life for custodians
headings.reviewNote: Sets twenty years to life and fine up to two hundred fifty thousand dollars for child under eighteen, life without probation or parole until twenty-five years served for force, abduction, or coercion, and natural-life term for parent, legal guardian, or custodian.

entries.reviewSummary: Dual-version entry (H.B. 2273, et al., 2026; Revisor note states effective 8-28-26); subsection 3 has 25-year minimum for force/abduction/coercion in (1) and natural-life term for parent/guardian/custodian in (2).

headings.title: Definition and elements of sexual trafficking of a child in the second degree
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense as recruiting, harboring, causing, or advertising child under eighteen to participate in commercial sex, sexual performance, or explicit material.

headings.title: Belief of child's age of eighteen or older not a defense
headings.reviewNote: Provides that defendant's belief that child was eighteen years of age or older is not a defense.

headings.title: Felony penalty range and eighty-five percent mandatory minimum under section 558.011
headings.reviewNote: Sets twenty years to life and fine up to two hundred fifty thousand dollars for child under eighteen, and life without probation or parole until eighty-five percent served under section 558.011 for force, abduction, or coercion; omits separate custodian subdivision.

entries.reviewSummary: Dual-version entry (H.B. 2273 merged with H.B. 2637 & 3155, 2026; Revisor note states effective 1-01-28); subsection 3 replaces 25-year minimum with 85% under section 558.011 and omits separate custodian subdivision.

headings.title: Definition and elements of contributing to human trafficking through misuse of documentation
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense as destroying, concealing, or confiscating passport or ID, or restricting travel to maintain labor or services.

headings.title: Exemption from sexual offender registration requirements
headings.reviewNote: Exempts person convicted of misuse of documentation from sex offender registration under section 589.400 unless otherwise required.

headings.title: Class E felony classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies offense of contributing to human trafficking through misuse of documentation as a class E felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text (effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Mandatory victim restitution for human trafficking offenses
headings.reviewNote: Mandates court order of restitution compensating victim for labor value and physical and mental rehabilitation of victim and children.

headings.title: Seizure and civil forfeiture of property under section 513.607
headings.reviewNote: Permits seizure of defendant's real or personal property used, attempted to be used, or intended to be used in trafficking offenses, and mandates forfeiture under section 513.607 if seized.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified against archived text (2026 amendment); distinguished permissive seizure ('may be seized') from mandatory forfeiture ('shall be forfeited') in subsection 2 note.

headings.title: Application of federal Trafficking Victims Protection Act rights and protections
headings.reviewNote: Affords victims alleging state human trafficking violations all rights and protections in federal Trafficking Victims Protection Act of 2000.

headings.title: Affirmative defense of physical coercion for prostitution charges
headings.reviewNote: Establishes affirmative defense to prostitution charge under section 567.020 where conduct was coerced by unlawful physical force.

headings.title: Department of public safety victim identification procedures and training protocols
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department of public safety to establish victim identification procedures, training programs, and inter-agency protocols.

headings.title: Law enforcement notification to social services and juvenile justice authorities
headings.reviewNote: Requires law enforcement to notify department of social services and juvenile authorities upon encountering suspected trafficking victim.

headings.title: Department of social services victim services coordination and housing contracts
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department of social services to coordinate victim services and contract with shelters and nonprofits for housing and rehabilitation.

headings.title: Civil cause of action by trafficking victim for damages and attorney fees
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes trafficking victim to bring civil action for actual damages, attorney fees, and punitive damages within ten-year limitation period.

headings.title: Attorney general civil action for penalties up to fifty thousand dollars and equitable relief
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes attorney general to bring civil action for injunctive relief and civil penalties up to fifty thousand dollars per violation dedicated to victim restitution.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text and Revisor transfer footnotes (*578.475, **566.210/566.211); preserved permissive vs mandatory distinctions across subsections 3-7.
